claims.text: An Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA with VEC below 4.5 and discrete B2 precipitates in a continuous BCC matrix will combine high strength, improved room-temperature ductility, and reduced density.
The proposed alloy will have yield strength above 1000 MPa at room temperature.
The proposed alloy will exhibit tensile elongation above 10% at room temperature.
The proposed alloy will have density below 10 g/cm3.
Equiatomic or near-equiatomic Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr has density above 12 g/cm3.
Equiatomic or near-equiatomic Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr has poor room-temperature ductility because of a continuous B2 phase or brittle intermetallics.
Replacing high-density Ta with lower-density Ti and Mo reduces RHEA density.
Adjusting elemental ratios to VEC below 4.5 promotes a single-phase BCC or inverted BCC+B2 microstructure.
Thermomechanical processing such as hot isostatic pressing or rapid solidification can produce the desired single-phase BCC or inverted BCC+B2 microstructure.
Trace Al or Cr additions can stabilize discrete B2 precipitates in the proposed alloy.
A continuous BCC matrix permits dislocation glide and thereby avoids catastrophic brittle fracture.
Discrete B2 precipitates provide precipitation strengthening while preserving improved room-temperature ductility.
Chemical short-range order impedes dislocation motion without causing catastrophic brittle fracture.
Chemical short-range order and phase-stability engineering suppress brittle intermetallic formation.
Single-phase BCC RHEAs made from subgroup IV, V, and VI metals are intrinsically ductile when VEC is below 4.5.
RHEAs with VEC at or above 4.6 are intrinsically brittle.
The VEC-dependent brittle-to-ductile transition arises because electronic-structure changes shift the elastic instability mode from tensile failure to shear failure.
A continuous ordered B2 matrix causes poor room-temperature ductility, whereas an inverted BCC-matrix/B2-precipitate structure improves ductility while maintaining high yield strength.
Excessive cooling rates can generate amorphous phases or undesirable secondary phases in the proposed alloy.

contradictions.description: The intervention permits either a single-phase BCC structure or an inverted BCC+B2 structure, but the boundary states that the microstructure must be inverted and that B2 precipitates are necessary.
